    Literal powers of closed quiver paths #

    BGRS writes powers of a selected closed path literally. Keep that combinatorial datum separate from the weaker assertion that an arbitrary path has the same image as a power. Reversed path evaluation sends a literal path power to the corresponding endomorphism power.

    source
    theorem Quiver.Path.loopPow_one {Q : Type u} [Quiver Q] {i : Q} (p : Path i i) :
    p.loopPow 1 = p
    source
    theorem Quiver.Path.loopPow_succ_left {Q : Type u} [Quiver Q] {i : Q} (p : Path i i) (n : ℕ) :
    p.loopPow (n + 1) = p.comp (p.loopPow n)

    The same successor power with the new copy displayed on the left.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.LinearPathCategory.pathMap_loopPow {Q : Type v} [Quiver Q] {C : Type z} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_1, z} C] (F₀ : Q → C) (F₁ : {i j : Q} → (i ⟶ j) → (F₀ j ⟶ F₀ i)) {i : Q} (p : Quiver.Path i i) (n : ℕ) :
    pathMap F₀ (fun {i j : Q} => F₁) (p.loopPow n) = CategoryTheory.End.of (pathMap F₀ (fun {i j : Q} => F₁) p) ^ n

    Reversed path evaluation respects literal powers of a closed path.
